markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the law is enacted
markets.rules_primary: If the 2027 state budget (loi de finances pour 2027) is enacted in France before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
“The 2027 budget” means the loi de finances pour 2027, France’s annual State finance law for 2027. Final adoption by Parliament, including a text deemed adopted under Article 49, paragraph 3, of the Constitution, does NOT count until the President promulgates the law, which follows any review by the Constitutional Council. The market resolves to Yes if the promulgated law bears a date of Dec 31, 2026 or earlier, as shown by its publication in the Journal officiel de la République française.

A special law (loi spéciale) that only authorizes the collection of existing taxes and borrowing, or any other interim measure of that kind, does not count. The social security financing law (loi de financement de la sécurité sociale) is a separate law and does not count.

The 2027 budget put into force by ordinance under Article 47 of the Constitution counts once the ordinance has been signed and published in the Journal officiel.

Enactment requires completion of all constitutional and legal requirements for the legislation to become binding law.

Standard legislation requiring executive approval: final passage by all required legislative bodies, executive signature OR becoming law despite executive inaction OR successful veto override, and satisfaction of any required waiting periods
Legislation not requiring executive approval: final passage and completion of required waiting periods
Constitutional amendments: passage with required supermajorities and completion of ratification processes
Executive orders: official signature, publication in official government records, and legal effectiveness

The following do NOT constitute enactment:

Legislative passage without completed executive action
Passage by only some required bodies
Provisional passage
Non-binding resolutions
Draft orders

Enactment occurs when all requirements are completed, regardless of pending judicial challenges.

markets.rules_secondary:
The Prime Minister formally engaging the Government's responsibility under Article 49, paragraph 3 of the French Constitution on the 2027 state budget bill, or the Government officially announcing that it will do so, qualifies. Engagement on any part of the bill (such as the first part, covering revenue) or at any reading (including on a joint committee text or in a new reading) qualifies. Engagement only on the 2027 social security financing bill (projet de loi de financement de la sécurité sociale) does not qualify. A motion of censure being filed, adopted or rejected afterwards does not change the result. Statements that the Government may or could use Article 49.3 do not qualify until it is engaged or officially announced.

An agreement or announcement qualifies if it involves any of the following:

Formal signing of treaties
Parliamentary approval with binding effect
Official ratification
Formal commitment by the head of state/government with constitutional authority
Official statements by authorized ministers
Official press releases
Formal declarations during government proceedings
Official statements to international bodies

Phased implementation announcements and multi-party agreements where the country is a signatory also qualify.

The following do NOT qualify:

Preliminary discussions
Conditional agreements contingent on circumstances
Opposition party statements
Leaked documents
Think-tank recommendations
General aspirations without specific commitment
Draft legislation without approval
Regional actions (unless specified)

markets.rules_primary: If legislation establishing the Canada Strong Fund has become law in Canada before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
“Legislation establishing the Canada Strong Fund” means an Act of Parliament that creates, incorporates, or grants statutory authority for the Canada Strong Fund, or for a Crown corporation or substantially similar federal entity whose stated purpose is to operate the Canada Strong Fund.

Enactment requires completion of all constitutional and legal requirements for the legislation to become binding law.

Standard legislation requiring executive approval: final passage by all required legislative bodies, executive signature OR becoming law despite executive inaction OR successful veto override, and satisfaction of any required waiting periods
Legislation not requiring executive approval: final passage and completion of required waiting periods
Constitutional amendments: passage with required supermajorities and completion of ratification processes
Executive orders: official signature, publication in official government records, and legal effectiveness

The following do NOT constitute enactment:

Legislative passage without completed executive action
Passage by only some required bodies
Provisional passage
Non-binding resolutions
Draft orders

Enactment occurs when all requirements are completed, regardless of pending judicial challenges.

Note: This event was issued before the September 14, 2026 amendment to the LAW Contract, so that amendment does not apply. To be clear, a law must take legal effect before this event’s deadline; a law enacted before the deadline whose effective date falls on or after it does not satisfy the Payout Criterion.

For the purposes of this contract, enactment is satisfied upon the bill receiving Royal Assent in the United Kingdom; corresponding legislation or formal consent by Commonwealth realms is not required.

Enactment requires completion of all constitutional and legal requirements for the legislation to become binding law. For executive orders, this includes official signature, publication in official government records, and legal effectiveness. markets.rules_primary: If Anthropic announces a complete solution, developed by Anthropic or researchers collaborating directly with Anthropic on that solution, to one of the six Millennium Prize Problems unsolved as of September 5, 2026 before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The qualifying announcement must expressly state that Anthropic developed or co-developed the solution, or expressly identify outside researchers as having collaborated with Anthropic on developing that solution.

The qualifying problems are the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture, Hodge Conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, P versus NP, Riemann Hypothesis, and Yang-Mills existence and mass gap problem.

Work by an independent Claude user does NOT count, even if Anthropic publicizes it. Providing model access or research credits alone is not direct collaboration on the solution. Partial results, numerical evidence, or formalization of a previously known solution do NOT count as a complete solution.

Clay acceptance, peer review, and a prize award are not required.

markets.rules_primary: If the number of calendar days on which an RTO-wide PJM Maximum Generation Emergency/Load Management Alert – Capacity Emergency – NERC EEA 1 was applicable in 2026 is above 12 days, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A calendar day counts once if the specified emergency procedure was applicable for any portion of that day, regardless of how many separate postings were issued. Only postings applying to PJM-RTO will count; emergencies limited to individual zones or regions will not. Drills will not count.

PJM’s Postings Report explicitly counts an event on each date for which it is applicable, including events that span multiple calendar days

Clarification (09/02/26): PJM’s Postings Report identifies 11 eligible calendar days on which the specified alert was applicable through September 2. Although 12 non-drill days appear under “postings”, one of those dates, May 20, is excluded because the corresponding alert applied only to BGE, DOM, and PEPCO, rather than PJM-RTO. Drills are also excluded, and each qualifying calendar day is counted only once. Accordingly, the current resolution value is 11 qualifying days, and the “Above 10 days” market will be determined Yes. The other strikes remain undetermined.

markets.rules_primary:
If the highest standard Disneyland one-day, one-park adult ticket price on December 31, 2026 at 12:00 PM ET is above 

$216, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This market uses the upper endpoint of the standard one-day, one-park ticket price range published on Disneyland Resort’s official ticketing page for guests ages 10 and older. If the page no longer displays a range, the highest official price across standard date-based tiers for admission to Disneyland Park in Anaheim, California, will be used.

The price must be in effect at the observation time. Prices for future admission dates, including dates in 2027, count; announced increases not yet in effect do not. Sold-out reservation dates do not disqualify an otherwise published tier price.

Prices are in USD, excluding taxes, fees, discounts, Park Hopper, Lightning Lane, special events, partial-day tickets, multi-day tickets, annual passes, and packages. Only the price at the observation time counts; earlier prices do not determine settlement.

This market and these products have not been endorsed by Disney Enterprises, Inc. or its affiliates. Any references to Disneyland, Disneyland Resort, Disney, or any associated marks are descriptive only and do not indicate an endorsement of this product or any affiliation between Disney Enterprises, Inc. or its affiliates and Kalshi.

markets.rules_primary: If Troy Jackson's certified vote share in the 2026 general election is lower than Kamala Harris's certified 2024 presidential vote share in their state, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A candidate's 2026 vote share is their share of all votes cast in the November 3, 2026 general election for the listed office, as certified by that state's official election authority, including votes received on every ballot line on which the candidate appears. Where a race uses ranked-choice tabulation or a runoff, the first-round (first-choice) share is used. Kamala Harris's 2024 vote share is her share of that state's certified 2024 presidential vote, including every ballot line on which she appeared, per the Federal Election Commission's official 2024 presidential general election results. Shares are compared unrounded.

Offices: Troy Jackson, U.S. Senate (Maine); Tina Kotek, Governor (Oregon); Keisha Lance Bottoms, Governor (Georgia); Kathy Hochul, Governor (New York); Chris Pappas, U.S. Senate (New Hampshire); Abdul El-Sayed, U.S. Senate (Michigan); Angie Nixon, U.S. Senate (Florida); David Jolly, Governor (Florida); Peggy Flanagan, U.S. Senate (Minnesota). A market resolves NO if the listed person is not the Democratic nominee (for Minnesota, the Democratic-Farmer-Labor nominee) on that race's 2026 general-election ballot.

markets.rules_primary: If the certified percentage of the popular vote received by Jack Reed in the 2026 Rhode Island Senate election is 72% to 100%, inclusive of both endpoints, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: The percentage is calculated as (total votes received by Jack Reed ÷ total valid votes cast) × 100, rounded to two decimal places. Except as provided in the Contract, resolution is based on certified/official results only, not preliminary results. Write-in votes are included if they appear in certified results. Invalid, spoiled, or rejected ballots are excluded from both numerator and denominator.
